n: Psalm 43 continues Psalm 42 — it has no title and repeats the same refrain, so many think they were once a single song. The psalmist asks God to defend him against a faithless people and a lying man.

f.g: A people without ḥesed (covenant loyalty) — faithless.

n: He knows God is his fortress, yet he feels rejected. He repeats the question from Psalm 42: why must I go around mourning?

He asks God to send light and truth as guides, like messengers that will lead him home to the holy mountain and the temple. Latter-day revelation connects light and truth with intelligence and the Spirit.

f.g: Mount Zion in Jerusalem, where the temple stood.

n: Once there, he will go to the altar and praise God — his greatest joy — with music. The longing of Psalm 42 turns to anticipation.

f.g: Literally “God, the gladness of my joy.”

n: For the third time the refrain sounds. The questions remain, but the answer is firm: hope in God, for I will praise him again.
